newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins higher but trade still nervous.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins higher but trade still nervous.

text.p: Prices of Russian MinFin bonds firmed on generally positive news from Russia and a rise in other emerging market debt but dealers said trading remained thin on fears of a possible freezing of further bonds.
Russian police are preparing an order to freeze up to a further $7 million nominal of MinFin bonds, which have been stolen.
Dealers said Russian operators were buying speculatively with deals mainly struck through brokers to reduce the risk in nervous trading.
"There has been buying, prices have risen but many Russian and foreign operators are not trading yet," an ICFI Moscow partners bank dealer said.
Dealers said today's rise could be due to firmer Vnesh debt prices and those of other emerging markets.
Fading concerns about President Boris Yeltsin's health and the troop withdrawal from the Chechen capital Grozny were also positive, they added.
"MinFins were supposed to rise due to all these things but the liquidity is still lower as it is not clear if more bonds will be frozen or not," one dealer said.
"But there is no panic, nobody is selling, maybe potential investors are just scared off the market," he added.
